meta.name: andalus
meta.description: One person's Windows terminal environment, expressed as data instead of as a script.
notes: JSON rather than YAML for this document because ConvertFrom-Json is built into every supported engine, and a fresh machine has no YAML parser. The winget file next to this one is YAML only because winget requires it, and this project never parses it.

Font sha256 values are intentionally blank. Fetching an archive over TLS proves who served it, not what it contains. apply must refuse to install a font whose hash is blank rather than trusting the transport, so filling these in is a prerequisite for apply rather than a nice-to-have.

terminal.global, shell.profile, terminal.asset and omp.theme are resource kinds this build does not model. They are left in deliberately: plan reports them as unverified, which is the behaviour that stops a partial plan from reading like a converged machine.

The Andalus palette is authored, not derived. Its sixteen colours come from manuscript illumination pigments: lapis lazuli for blue, gold leaf for yellow, vermilion for red, Persian turquoise for cyan, aubergine for purple, on a parchment foreground. The Volcanic Heat scheme it replaces had fourteen of its sixteen colours guessed. None of these are.

The prompt contains no Arabic words, and that is deliberate. Windows Terminal renders Arabic left to right even where it shapes and joins the letters correctly, so any Arabic string in a prompt displays reversed, and displays differently across builds. The theme uses three standalone ornaments from Arabic Presentation Forms instead: U+FD3E and U+FD3F ornate parentheses, and U+06DE start of Rub el Hizb. All three are bidi class Other Neutral with no joining behaviour, so they render the same in every direction context. Arabic calligraphy reaches the window as a background image, where it is pixels and bidi never applies.

The prompt now depends on Nerd Font glyphs. This reverses an earlier decision recorded here, and the reversal is not free. The rounded segment caps U+E0B6 and U+E0B4, and the os, folder, branch and clock icons, all live in the Private Use Area and exist only in a patched font. On a machine where the font resource has not been applied yet the prompt renders as replacement boxes, which is a real bootstrap ordering problem the previous zero-glyph design did not have. doctor verifying that the font family is genuinely installed is therefore load-bearing now rather than informational.

The frosted panels behind the text in the reference image are not a Windows Terminal capability. Terminal paints one uniform character grid: there is no per-region background, no rounded rectangle and no drop shadow anywhere in the settings schema. Those panels have to be painted into the background image. This fixes the requirement for the asset: a dark translucent wash across the left two thirds so text stays legible, with the artwork weighted to the right.

backgroundImage composites on top of the acrylic layer rather than beneath it, so image opacity and window frosting trade against each other directly. At backgroundImageOpacity 1.0 the blur is completely hidden and the window is frosted only in the settings file. 0.85 is the compromise being tested.

useAcrylic with opacity 72 is a request, not a guarantee. Windows ignores it when Transparency effects are turned off in Settings, and suppresses it under Battery Saver. doctor must report the effective state rather than the requested one, because a converged terminal.fragment is not the same thing as a window that actually looks frosted.
